title: On-Prem Kubernetes Ops Playbook — vSphere & Bare Metal + Terraform Notes
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures the recommended operational steps, Terraform module notes, and upgrade approach for on-prem Kubernetes clusters we run for Private deployments (vSphere + bare metal). It is intended for SREs and platform engineers who own cluster provisioning, upgrades, and incident recovery.

Scope / Audience:
- Clusters deployed in customer datacenters or on-prem racks and in vSphere managed environments.
- Focused on: initial bootstrap, Terraform-driven infra modules, controlled upgrades of controlplane and worker nodes, and rollback paths.
- Not covering hosted/cloud-managed services (EKS/GKE).

Assumptions:
- We manage etcd (self-hosted) for on-prem clusters; etcd backups are taken outside the kube control plane (snapshots to NFS/object store).
- Remote state for Terraform lives in an S3-compatible backend with locking (minio + DynamoDB or Consul lock).
- Secrets (VC credentials, TLS keys) are stored in Vault and referenced by Terraform via the Vault provider, not checked into git.

High-level architecture notes:
- Control plane: 3 nodes (HA) across fault domains when possible.
- Load balancing: HAProxy (on dedicated LBVMs) or MetalLB for BGP setups. For vSphere prefer NSX-T or vSphere LB if available.
- Storage: CSI drivers (vSphere CSI for vSphere; local-path/rook-ceph for bare metal).
- CNI: Calico for policy and IP management; consider Cilium for eBPF performance requirements.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any bootstrap/upgrade):
- DNS entries resolvable for api.cluster.local and node hostnames.
- NTP in sync across all hosts.
- vCenter user with required privileges (list below) present in Vault.
- BMC/IPMI credentials validated for bare-metal provisioning.
- Object store reachable and credentials valid for remote state and backups.
- Monitoring and alerting hooks configured (Prometheus, Alertmanager endpoints).

vSphere-specific notes:
- Required vCenter privileges: Datacenter.VM.create, Datastore.* read/write, Network.* attach, ContentLibrary.read, Folder.*. Keep a minimal role in Confluence.
- Use the vSphere CSI and CCM: enable CSI v2-compatible module; set datacenter and datastore attributes via Terraform variables.
- Tag VMs with cluster-id and node-role for lifecycle automation.
- Prefer using a dedicated vSphere cluster or resource pool per customer to avoid noisy_neighbor issues.
- When using vSphere with NSX-T, verify LBIP pools and NAT rules before cluster creation.

Bare metal-specific notes (PXE/iPXE flow):
- Bootflow recommended: iPXE -> preseed/cloud-init -> kubeadm join. Keep the installer image minimal and immutable.
- Use MAAS/Crowbar/Metal³ for hardware lifecycle where available; otherwise document manual BMC steps in runbook.
- Attach local SSDs for etcd if available for performance; separate etcd network recommended.

Terraform module patterns and notes (opinionated):
- Repo layout: terraform-modules/ (reusable modules) + infra-live/customer-x/ (live configs). Use terragrunt only if multiple layers needed, but prefer simple module composition.
- Module primitives: vsphere_vm, baremetal_node (ipmi), lb_instance, network_segment, datastore_config, dns_record.
- Inputs to standardize: cluster_id, environment, fault_domain, kube_version, ssh_pub_key, network_tags, datastore_name, storage_class_map (json string).
- Outputs: inventory_host_file (for ansible), control_plane_ips (list), lb_vip, datastore_ids.
- State: s3 backend with server_side_encryption = true and state locking enabled (DynamoDB or Consul). For fully air-gapped customers use a local Consul cluster with ACLs.
- Secrets: integrate vault provider; terraform should fetch vSphere credentials at runtime; do not render credentials into tfstate.
- Module versioning: release modules via semantic tags (v1.2.0) and pin module versions in infra-live via git tags.
- Testing: include a minimal terratest suite in each module to validate basic create/destroy in CI (against lab vSphere or KVM images).

Example Terraform variable snippet (for infra-live):
- var.cluster_id = "redwood-cust-42"
- var.kube_version = "1.27.6"
- var.control_plane_count = 3
- var.worker_count = 6
- var.vsphere_datastore = "fast-ssd-01"

Bootstrap / cluster creation workflow (recommended):
1) Create infra via Terraform (networks, lb, vms/datastores).
2) Generate TLS and kubeadm config via CI runner using Vault-templated artifacts.
3) Run kubeadm init (control plane) on first control node using the generated config, then kubeadm join for additional control plane nodes.
4) Apply CNI and CSI manifests (version-locked manifests from our manifests repo).
5) Join workers. Run post-install smoke tests: kubectl get nodes, run nginx pod, verify PVC binding.

Upgrade playbook (control plane + workers) — safe, canary approach:
- Goal: minimize downtime and allow quick rollback. Always assume backups exist.
- Pre-upgrade: capture etcd snapshot, export current manifests, take Prometheus targets snapshot, check cluster-level gating (PDBs, long-running jobs).
- Step 0: announce change window and update runbook in Slack #private-deployments.
- Step 1: Upgrade control plane one node at a time (cordon -> drain -> kubeadm upgrade apply -> uncordon) with at least one control plane left serving API. Verify API health (kubectl get cs, /healthz) before proceeding.
- Step 2: Run kube-controller-manager and scheduler smoke checks, confirm kube-apiserver metrics stable.
- Step 3: Upgrade kube-proxy, CNI components via DaemonSet rolling update or manifest apply.
- Step 4: Upgrade workers in small batches (2–3 nodes) with cordon->drain->upgrade kubelet/kubectl -> kubeadm upgrade node -> uncordon. Verify workloads restart correctly and PVCs remount.
- Canary step: if using dedicated customer-facing nodes, upgrade a canary pool first for 24–48 hours and evaluate logs/metrics.
- Post-upgrade: run integration tests (CRD reconciliation, latency-sensitive endpoints), run perf smoke tests for tail-latency.

Rollback strategy (fast vs full):
- Fast rollback (control-plane minor fail): restore etcd snapshot (follow documented etcd restore steps) and point kube-api to previous certs if necessary; revert frontend LB to previous backend set.
- Full rollback: restore from infrastructure snapshot (VM snapshots) + etcd snapshot. This requires a larger recovery window and should be coordinated with customer.

Validation and verification checklist after any change:
- kubectl get nodes shows Ready for all nodes.
- kube-system pods running and not in CrashLoopBackOff.
- CSI and CNI pods healthy and PDs mounted.
- End-to-end app test: sample write/read from stateful app (MySQL/Postgres) and confirm retention.
- Latency tests: tail latency for inference route does not regress beyond 20% of baseline.
- Logs: no surge in errors for 30 minutes post-change.

Observability / runbook hooks:
- Dashboards: control-plane-latency, etcd-operation-duration, kubelet-restarts, CSI-errors.
- Alerts to tune: APIServerHighLatency (>500ms p95), etcd_quorum_lost, NodeNotReady (>5m).
- Tracing: ensure traces for control plane requests are sampled at 5% during upgrades for diagnostics.

Known gotchas and notes from past runs:
- vSphere CSI versions are picky: always test CSI version compatibility matrix with vSphere release.
- Kubeadm token TTLs can cause join races in automated flows; prefer pre-generated kubeadm join tokens with long TTL for bootstrap pipelines.
- Terraform drift observed when cloud-init changes node metadata post-provision; prefer idempotent cloud-init snippets.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide on long-term recommendation: Calico vs Cilium for customers with heavy L7/sidecar workloads.
- Add Terratest lab for bare-metal ipmi flows (queue with infra).
- Draft a succinct customer-facing KB for scheduled upgrades and expected maintenance windows.

Appendix A — Quick etcd snapshot/restore commands (ops copy):
- Snapshot: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=${ETCD_ENDPOINTS} snapshot save /backup/etcd-$(date +%F-%s).db --cert=/etc/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/etcd/peer.key --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.crt
- Restore: etcdctl snapshot restore /backup/etcd-last.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd-restored --initial-cluster "..." (follow full restore doc).

Appendix B — Minimal Terraform module checklist for PR reviews:
- Accepts cluster_id and kube_version as vars.
- Uses remote state backend configured via env vars.
- Does not inline secrets; uses vault provider.
- Has outputs needed for ansible/bootstrapping.
- Documented upgrade path in module README.

Notes to future self: keep this doc lightweight; move stable runbook fragments into Confluence (linked above) and keep Terraform module design details in the module READMEs. This Drive doc is intentionally an iterative working reference for engineering teams running on-prem/private deployments.
